hook.title: Walking the cliff edge with a shaky hand
hook.text: You must walk to a goal along a cliff. **Q-learning** plans as if it will always step perfectly: the shortest path hugs the edge. **SARSA** knows its own hand shakes (it *really does* explore randomly 10% of the time) and learns the value of the policy *it actually follows*, so it prefers a path with a safety margin. Same notebook, different target: Q-learning bootstraps from the *best* next action, SARSA from the action it *actually chose* next.
hook.recall: Remember the shaky hand: Q-learning (off-policy) uses $\max_{a'}Q(s',a')$ in its target; SARSA (on-policy) uses $Q(s',a')$ for the next action actually chosen by its own ε-greedy policy.

explore.intro: Cliff walking: −1 per step, −100 for falling (back to start). Both agents explore with ε-greedy.
tasks: Compare the two greedy paths at $\varepsilon=0.1$. Which hugs the cliff edge?
Set $\varepsilon=0$. Do the paths still differ?
explore.takeaway: Q-learning target: $r+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s',a')$. SARSA target: $r+\gamma Q(s',a')$ with $a'$ chosen by the policy. (The slides show the cliff figure with “optimal path” and “safer path”; which algorithm learns which is textbook context.)
